newsitem.title: UK: Metals end week marking time, LME locks in gains.
newsitem.headline: Metals end week marking time, LME locks in gains.

text.p: Activity slowed during Friday afternoon LME trading, with the base metal complex's leading performers settling into a consolidatory mode, traders said.
After an initial upward flurry, prices drifted back and did little from midsession onwards.
"It looked as if there was going to be some followthrough, but then they all just drifted off. There is resistance at the top of the ranges," one trader said.
In copper, the early jump to a new 11-1/2 month high of $2,488 was not sustained, and with the cash/threes backwardation narrowing, the market fell away.
Conditions quietened also, and by the end of the kerb three months was back at $2,466, up just $3 from Thursday's kerb.
Traders see the market favouring the upside still, with continued concerns over labour disruption and drought conditions in Chile a key factor in a tight market.
Next week, the market will focus on nearby prompts, such as "third Wednesday".
"We will be trading for the May date on Monday, so there may be some excitement there," the trader said.
Elsewhere, similar slack conditions prevailed during the latter part of the day, with aluminium struggling to erode resistsance above $1,670.
Nevertheless, a contraction in the contango, due to nearby borrowing helped keep the market in the plus column. Last business was at $1,666.50, up $8.50.
Cash/threes narrowed in to $18/19, against Thursday's $23.50. Financing levels are just above $30.
Nickel kept a close eye on developments at Inco's Sudbury operations, ahead of the May 31 labour contract expiry.
Overnight, workers voted for a strike mandate, although, the company were optimistic that a new three year contract would be agreed.
Prices were also assisted by an 888-tonne fall in LME stocks, but the upmove was fairly limited. Last business was at $7,820, up $50.
Lead was quiet for most of the session, but sparked to life slightly during the latter part of the day. Prices edged up on the kerb to end at $630, a $4 advance from yesterday.
Zinc was supported on price dips, but largely consolidated after reaching fresh 4-1/2 year highs on Thursday. Last trade was at $1,348, up $4.
Tin traded in a tight $25 range, which kept interest at a minimum, and last business was at $5,760, down $10.
The alloy market was steady, when traded, and closed at $1,515/1,517.
